findings.title: Reschedules bypass deferred email cancellation
findings.body: Passing `true` selects the immediate-cancellation branch in `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`, which sends the SendGrid cancel request now instead of marking the reminder `cancelled` for the hourly-window cron. SendGrid keeps canceled scheduled sends pending until their scheduled date, and the cron will not find these rows because they are never marked cancelled. Reschedules far ahead can therefore consume the 100-pending-cancellation limit again, causing later cancellations to fail and reminders to be sent.

findings.title: The cancellation marker update is not awaited
findings.body: This call starts an async helper that marks the email reminder `cancelled` in the database, but the surrounding `forEach` discards its promise. The handler's later `Promise.all` does not include these helper calls, so it can finish before the marker is committed. If the cron runs before that update completes, it will not find the reminder and the scheduled email can still be sent. Await the reminder-cancellation operations before completing the handler.

findings.title: One SendGrid failure aborts all remaining cancellations
findings.body: The SendGrid request is inside a single `try` surrounding the entire loop. If any one request fails, iteration stops and the `Promise.all` that executes the queued reminder deletions is skipped, so later cancelled reminders are not attempted in this run. Since this cron runs every 15 minutes, a reminder due before the next run can still be sent, and previously processed rows will also be retried. Handle failures per reminder so one failure does not block independent cancellations.
